updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Adaptive Scope Evaluation with Lifecycle Status Control
updates.summary: Administrators will gain explicit control over how Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes evaluate recipient and site owner lifecycle states, ensuring policy targeting remains accurate as organizational membership changes. This enhancement helps prevent policies from inadvertently applying to or missing users whose status has changed.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Sensitivity Labels for Microsoft Entra Security Groups
updates.summary: Sensitivity labels published in Purview can now be applied directly to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups, extending classification and governance capabilities without requiring separate label configuration. This unifies label management across M365 groups, sites, and Entra security groups.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management - Priority Cleanup with Secure Workflow
updates.summary: A new secure workflow for Data Lifecycle Management enables administrators to create recurring exceptions to delete items under retention policies and legal holds, requiring a dedicated security role, multiple approvers, and full audit trail. This feature provides controlled, auditable access to bypass retention policies while maintaining compliance oversight.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint DLP Expansion for AI Agent Interactions
updates.summary: Microsoft Purview DLP is expanding inline protection to local AI agents, allowing organizations to enforce DLP policies on prompts, files, and tool interactions to prevent sensitive data exposure across human-to-agent and agent-to-tool workflows. Admins can now apply data loss prevention controls at supported agent interaction points.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint DLP Integration with Azure Firewall
updates.summary: Purview DLP now extends data security controls to the network layer by integrating with Azure Firewall, enabling detection and enforcement of DLP policies on network traffic including text, files, and AI interactions from servers, VMs, and automated workloads. This provides network-level protection for sensitive data in transit across cloud applications and APIs.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Improved Sensitive Information Types
updates.summary: Microsoft is enhancing its out-of-the-box sensitive information types (SITs) to identify and classify sensitive data with greater precision and reliability. These improvements help admins reduce false positives and strengthen data discovery accuracy across DLP and compliance policies.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Recurring Classifier Refresh
updates.summary: On-Demand Classification is being evolved into recurring classification refreshes that automatically update the classification of existing content as data and organizational context change over time. This reduces manual effort and keeps data classifications current and compliant with updated policies.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Automatic Data Preservation for High-Risk Users
updates.summary: Adaptive Protection in Purview now integrates insider risk levels with Data Lifecycle Management to automatically apply retention labels based on a user's risk profile, automatically moving users in and out of policies as their risk status changes. This enables proactive data preservation for users exhibiting suspicious behavior.

updates.title: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint DLP - FTP and SFTP Transfer Protection
updates.summary: Endpoint DLP now monitors sensitive data transferred over FTP and SFTP protocols and can apply restrictive actions based on organizational policies, closing a gap in legacy file transfer method monitoring. Organizations can configure FTP and SFTP activities directly in Endpoint DLP policies.

updates.title: CVE-2026-105590: Windows Active Directory Certificate Services Security Feature Bypass
updates.summary: An improper certificate validation flaw in Windows Active Directory Certificate Services allows authorized attackers to bypass security features over the network, potentially compromising certificate-based authentication and trust validation. Identity and security admins should prioritize patching systems running ADCS.

updates.title: CVE-2026-121680: Windows NTLM Spoofing Vulnerability
updates.summary: A spoofing vulnerability in Windows NTLM authentication allows attackers to impersonate users or systems under certain conditions, potentially compromising identity verification and access control mechanisms. Microsoft has extended patches to include Microsoft Office software, so admins should update both OS and Office components.

updates.title: CVE-2026-109467: Azure DevOps Server Remote Code Execution
updates.summary: An improper authentication vulnerability in Azure DevOps Server allows authorized attackers to execute arbitrary code over the network, potentially leading to compromise of CI/CD pipelines and source code repositories. Organizations using on-premises Azure DevOps Server should apply security updates immediately.

updates.title: CVE-2026-109455: Microsoft SharePoint Information Disclosure
updates.summary: An incorrect authorization flaw in Microsoft SharePoint allows authorized users to disclose sensitive information over the network, potentially exposing confidential documents or metadata beyond their intended access scope. Admins should review SharePoint permissions and apply available patches.

updates.title: CVE-2026-62903: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient Authentication Bypass
updates.summary: A capture-replay authentication bypass vulnerability in Microsoft.Data.SqlClient allows unauthorized attackers to disclose information from SQL Server over the network by replaying captured credentials. Applications using this library should update to patched versions to prevent credential compromise.

updates.title: CVE-2026-105588: Windows DHCP Server Elevation of Privilege
updates.summary: A missing authentication flaw in Windows DHCP Server allows authorized local attackers to escalate privileges on a system running the DHCP Server role, potentially leading to complete system compromise. Organizations should patch DHCP servers, particularly those exposed to untrusted networks.
